title: nail reads its fasta and hmm inputs through libsail's `Framed`
body:
`nail/src/io` frames, indexes and parses nail's inputs itself. `Database<R: RecordParser>` in `database.rs` builds an `IndexMap<String, Offset>` keyed by record name. It holds one `File` and reads a record back with a seek and a `read_exact` into a shared buffer, so `get(&mut self, key: &str)` takes `&mut self`. `Fasta` is `Database<FastaParser>` and `P7Hmm` is `Database<P7HmmParser>`. Parallel iteration in `impl_rayon.rs` clones the `Database` once per split, and each clone reopens the file.

## Proposal

The design under discussion with the sail side adds a struct named `Framed<S: Source>` to `libsail`. It holds a byte source and an `Index`, and `record(n)` returns the raw bytes of record `n`. nail wraps it:

```rust
pub struct Fasta(Framed<MmapSource>);

impl Fasta {
    pub fn open(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self>;
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize;
    pub fn position(&self, name: &[u8]) -> Result<Option<usize>>;
    pub fn get(&self, n: usize) -> Result<Sequence>;
}
```

`open` maps the file and builds the name index. `get` reads `record(n)` and parses it with `Sequence::from_fasta(&[u8])`, which takes over the body of `FastaParser::parse`. `P7Hmm` is the same struct over `Format::Hmm`, with the body of `P7HmmParser::parse` moved to a function that builds a `Profile` from record bytes. `get` takes `&self`, so parallel iteration needs no clones:

```rust
(0..db.len()).into_par_iter().map(|i| db.get(i))
```

## Cost

- `database.rs`, `fasta.rs`, `p7hmm.rs` and `impl_rayon.rs` under `nail/src/io` are removed.
- nail gains a dependency on `libsail`.
- A lookup by name becomes `position` followed by `get`. Callers such as `targets.get(&seed.seq)` change.
- A file truncated while it is mapped raises SIGBUS. nail's inputs are read-only, and nail's docs need one line saying so.

## Open

- `Framed` does not exist yet. This issue waits on `libsail` shipping it, and foam cannot record a dependency on another repository.
- `Index::build` walks a streaming `Reader`, which copies the mapped bytes through a buffer. Nobody has measured whether that is slower than nail's own index pass.
